page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes an L3 cache size of 33 MB. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-standard-2 sits in the lower performance tiers for most compute and memory operations. Its stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1398.19, placing it in the bottom 25%, while its multi-core score of 1837.38 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show poor throughput, with read-only large block transfers registering at 13.8 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.79 GB/sec. However, single-threaded gzip compression performance is average, reaching 23.81 GB/sec.

Due to its limited resource footprint, the instance exhibits poor performance in demanding tasks. Geekbench software compilation with clang scored 1704.0, and ray tracing scored 1369.0, both in the bottom 10%. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.95 GB/sec, and LLM inference for a small 135M model processes prompts at 100.65 tokens/sec. The qualitative cost profile of this instance reflects its entry-level general-purpose hardware class, offering a low-cost entry point for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, simple text processing, and low-intensity background tasks rather than database operations or heavy computational jobs.
